title: Wipe fingerprints off a desktop monitor without sliding it off the desk
instruction: Wipe every fingerprint off the monitor glass with the cloth. Leave the monitor standing on the desk, and let go.
context: People wipe desktop monitors at a desk. This one stands 20 cm forward of the centre of the desk. The wipe has to stay on the glass, and the monitor has to be left standing when the hands come away. Walking the foot off the desk scores nothing.
setup: Standard bimanual YAM with parallel grippers. Laminate desk 1.10 m deep by 1.30 m wide by 60 mm, centred at (0.36, 0, 0.7175), top at z = 0.7475 m. Coordinates in metres: x forward from the arm-base line, y to the robot's left, z up. The arm bases stay at the station height. Monitor: LG UltraGear 27GX790A (26.5 inch, 2560 x 1440, flat OLED), the SimReady articulation monitor_27gx790a at dataset revision e965976d90f025237ad9ea8881f5f82755f26d9d. With the stand, 605.2 x 579.3 x 249.1 mm and 9.3 kg at full height; the head alone is 605.2 x 351.0 x 45.3 mm and 5.1 kg. The asset origin is the bottom of the foot, placed at (0.56, 0, 0.7485), 20 cm forward of the desk centre, and yawed 180 degrees so the glass faces the robot. The height slide starts on its lower stop, 110 mm down (authored travel 112.88 mm). The glass is the flat face at local x = 0.0531 m, normal +x, spanning local y ±0.2956 m and local z 0.2364 to 0.5732 m. In the world the foot's underside corners run from x 0.440 to 0.680 and y -0.150 to 0.150, and the glass stays inside the desktop. Eight oily fingerprints, each a 24 mm square and 1.2 mm thick, sit on the glass at local (0.0545, y, z) for y in {-0.24, -0.08, 0.08, 0.24} and z in {0.32, 0.50}. Soft microfiber sheet, 200 x 200 mm and 10 mm thick, about 60 g, lying on the desk at (0.14, 0, 0.7535). The left hand pushes the left edge toward the right so the sheet bunches, then the right hand pinches the pile. Arms start in READY with open grippers. One fixed layout, no jitter. The desk, floor, camera mast, lights and one overhead plus two wrist cameras are the standard station.
scoring: A fingerprint disappears when the gripper and the cloth are both on the glass, inside the circle of diameter 80 mm centred on that stain, within 25 mm of the glass surface. A point off the glass does not count. The fingerprint cube is then scaled away and hidden. 1.0: all 8 wiped and the monitor still upright (panel +Z within 45 degrees of world +Z). 0.5: 4 to 7 wiped, monitor upright. 0: fewer than 4 wiped, or the monitor has fallen (tilted past 45 degrees from vertical). Once the monitor falls, the score locks at 0 even if it recovers. Full success (1.0) ends the trial early.
run_limit: 2,400 joint-position control steps (2 minutes at 20 Hz).
reset_notes: Put the monitor back on its mark with the height slide at the lower stop and the tilt at 0, the cloth back at its start, and both arms at READY. The eight fingerprints are drawn again. Nothing is consumed. In simulation, reset restores the root pose, both joints and the score history.
fidelity: LG SimReady mesh with three rigid bodies, a height slide and a tilt hinge; not a stand-in. Gravity on, tilt held by 8 N·m friction (estimate), slide on lower stop with 40 N friction. Restitution 0.05, static friction 0.4. Fingerprints are visual marks; each hides when gripper and cloth are both on the glass within 80 mm of the stain centre. The cloth is a PhysX surface deformable, 200 mm square. Cables, glass fracture and smearing omitted.
scores: Dream-1 (dreamlabs/dream-1-beta): 0.0 (seed 1, 2400 steps, hit the step limit, model_out_dream/adhoc_e7bf52de.json). Scripted demo: 1.0 (all 8 stains cleaned, monitor upright, 1166 steps).
